- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots downward — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0 to +0.30), model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.30), model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 3–7% for next 2–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative — add 3–8% bias to forecast for 30d if sentiment < -0.30.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.50 to +0.20 in 3–5 days), model lags — adjust forecast 2–4 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- Model often overestimates short-term (1–7d) volatility when sentiment is negative — reduce forecast variance by 20–30% for 1–7d horizon.
